subject: math
title: Grade 3 Fractions: Equal Parts, Sets and Number Lines
seo_title: Grade 3 Fractions Math Worksheets (BC Curriculum, Free, Answer Key)
meta_desc: Free Grade 3 math worksheets on fractions: equal parts, naming halves to tenths, fractions of a set, comparing unit fractions and fractions on a number line. 100 questions with an answer key, following the BC curriculum.
key_big: A fraction needs equal parts. More parts means smaller parts.
key_sub: In 3/4, the whole has 4 equal parts and 3 are counted. 1/8 is smaller than 1/4, because eighths are smaller pieces than fourths.
body_html:
Equal parts

A fraction is part of a whole. The whole must be cut into equal parts: parts that are all the same size.

Equal partsNameOne part
2halvesone half, 12
3thirdsone third, 13
4fourthsone fourth, 14
5fifthsone fifth, 15
6sixthsone sixth, 16
8eighthsone eighth, 18
10tenthsone tenth, 110

Name a fraction

The bottom number tells how many equal parts make the whole. The top number tells how many parts you count.

Example

A bar has 5 equal parts. 2 are shaded. What fraction is shaded? What fraction is not shaded?

There are 5 equal parts, so the bottom number is 5. 2 are shaded and 5 − 2 = 3 are not.

Answer: 25 shaded, 35 not shaded

Fractions of a set

A fraction can be part of a group of things. The bottom number is how many things are in the whole group.

Example

What is 14 of 12?

Share the 12 into 4 equal groups. Each group has 3.

Answer: 3

Compare unit fractions

A unit fraction has 1 on top. More equal parts means smaller parts. So the bigger the bottom number, the smaller the fraction.

Example

Compare 18 and 14.

A whole cut into 4 equal parts has bigger parts than a whole cut into 8 equal parts.

Answer: 18 < 14

Fractions on a number line

The space from 0 to 1 is the whole. Cut it into equal spaces and count the spaces from 0.

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Calling unequal parts “fourths” or “thirds”Fractions need equal parts
Thinking 18 is bigger than 14 because 8 is bigger than 4More parts means smaller parts, so 18 < 14
Writing 23 for 2 green and 3 white countersThe bottom number is all the counters: 25
Counting tick marks on a number lineCount the spaces between the marks
Counting the lines instead of the partsA bar with 3 lines inside has 4 parts

faq.q: What fractions do Grade 3 students learn in BC?
faq.a: The BC Grade 3 math curriculum lists fraction concepts. Students learn that a fraction is part of a whole cut into equal parts, name fractions such as halves, thirds, fourths, eighths and tenths with shapes, sets and number lines, and compare unit fractions.
Both are one piece of the same whole. A pizza cut into 8 equal slices has smaller slices than a pizza cut into 4, so 1/8 < 1/4.

faq.q: What is a fraction of a set?
faq.a: It is part of a group of things. If 2 of 5 apples are red, then 2/5 of the apples are red, because the bottom number is all the apples.

faq.q: How can I help my child practise fractions at home?
faq.a: Cut sandwiches, pizza or paper into equal parts and name each part. Ask questions like “Is 1/3 or 1/6 of the pizza bigger?” and check that the parts are really equal.

items.q: How many equal parts does the bar have?
items.e: Count the parts, not the lines. The bar has 5 equal parts. (It has only 4 lines inside, because the ends are not cuts.)

items.q: How many equal parts does the circle have?
items.e: Count the parts, not the lines. The circle has 6 equal parts.

items.q: How many equal parts does the rectangle have?
items.e: Count the parts, not the lines. The rectangle has 8 equal parts.

items.q: How many equal parts does the bar have?
items.e: Count the parts, not the lines. The bar has 10 equal parts. (It has only 9 lines inside, because the ends are not cuts.)

items.q: The circle is cut into equal parts. What are the parts called?
items.e: There are 2 equal parts. 2 equal parts are called halves. We say halves, not “twos”.

items.q: The bar is cut into equal parts. What are the parts called?
items.e: There are 3 equal parts. 3 equal parts are called thirds.

items.q: The rectangle is cut into equal parts. What are the parts called?
items.e: There are 4 equal parts. 4 equal parts are called fourths.

items.q: The circle is cut into equal parts. What are the parts called?
items.e: There are 8 equal parts. 8 equal parts are called eighths.

No. It shows 13.
items.e: A fraction needs equal parts. These 2 parts are different sizes, so the shaded part is not 12.

No. It shows 15.

items.q: Which bar is cut into equal parts?
items.e: Equal parts are all the same size. That is picture D. A has 3 parts, but they are different sizes. B has 4 parts of different sizes. C has 2 parts of different sizes.

items.q: Which circle is cut into equal parts?
items.e: Equal parts are all the same size. That is picture C. A has 4 parts, but they are different sizes. B has 3 parts of different sizes. D has 2 parts of different sizes.

items.q: Which bar is cut into fourths?
items.e: Fourths are 4 equal parts. That is picture C. A has 4 parts, but they are not equal, so they are not fourths. B has 3 equal parts, which are thirds. D has 5 equal parts, which are fifths.

items.q: Which circle is cut into sixths?
items.e: Sixths are 6 equal parts. That is picture D. A has 6 parts, but they are not equal, so they are not sixths. B has 5 equal parts, which are fifths. C has 8 equal parts, which are eighths.

items.q: Nadia folds a square piece of paper in half. Then she folds it in half again. She opens it. How many equal parts are there?
items.e: The first fold makes 2 equal parts. The second fold cuts each of those in half: 2 × 2 = 4 equal parts.

items.q: Wei folds a paper strip in half, then in half again. What is each part called?
items.e: Two folds in half make 4 equal parts. Each part is one fourth, 14.

items.q: What fraction of the circle is shaded?
items.e: The circle has 2 equal parts, so the bottom number is 2. 1 part is shaded, so the top number is 1. The answer is 12.

items.q: What fraction of the bar is shaded?
items.e: The bar has 3 equal parts, so the bottom number is 3. 2 parts are shaded, so the top number is 2. The answer is 23. (21 compares shaded parts with white parts. The bottom number must be all the parts.)

items.q: What fraction of the rectangle is shaded?
items.e: The rectangle has 4 equal parts, so the bottom number is 4. 3 parts are shaded, so the top number is 3. The answer is 34. (31 compares shaded parts with white parts. The bottom number must be all the parts.)

items.q: What fraction of the bar is shaded?
items.e: The bar has 5 equal parts, so the bottom number is 5. 2 parts are shaded, so the top number is 2. The answer is 25. (23 compares shaded parts with white parts. The bottom number must be all the parts.)

items.q: What fraction of the circle is shaded?
items.e: The circle has 6 equal parts, so the bottom number is 6. 5 parts are shaded, so the top number is 5. The answer is 56. (51 compares shaded parts with white parts. The bottom number must be all the parts.)

items.q: What fraction of the rectangle is shaded?
items.e: The rectangle has 8 equal parts, so the bottom number is 8. 3 parts are shaded, so the top number is 3. The answer is 38. (35 compares shaded parts with white parts. The bottom number must be all the parts.)

items.q: What fraction of the bar is shaded?
items.e: The bar has 10 equal parts, so the bottom number is 10. 7 parts are shaded, so the top number is 7. The answer is 710. (73 compares shaded parts with white parts. The bottom number must be all the parts.)

items.q: What fraction of the rectangle is shaded?
items.e: The rectangle has 6 equal parts, so the bottom number is 6. 4 parts are shaded, so the top number is 4. The answer is 46. (42 compares shaded parts with white parts. The bottom number must be all the parts.)

items.q: What fraction of the circle is shaded?
items.e: The circle has 5 equal parts, so the bottom number is 5. 1 part is shaded, so the top number is 1. The answer is 15.

items.q: What fraction of the circle is not shaded?
items.e: There are 8 equal parts and 3 are shaded. 8 − 3 = 5 parts are not shaded, so the answer is 58.

items.q: What fraction of the rectangle is not shaded?
items.e: There are 10 equal parts and 4 are shaded. 10 − 4 = 6 parts are not shaded, so the answer is 610.

items.q: What fraction of the bar is not shaded?
items.e: There are 4 equal parts and 1 is shaded. 4 − 1 = 3 parts are not shaded, so the answer is 34.

items.q: Which picture shows 34 shaded?
items.e: 34 needs 4 equal parts with 3 shaded. That is picture C. A shows 14. B has 3 shaded and 4 white parts, so it shows 37. D has 4 parts, but they are not equal.

items.q: Which picture shows 25 shaded?
items.e: 25 needs 5 equal parts with 2 shaded. That is picture B. A shows 35. C has 5 parts, but they are not equal. D has 2 shaded and 5 white parts, so it shows 27.

items.q: Which picture shows 58 shaded?
items.e: 58 needs 8 equal parts with 5 shaded. That is picture A. B shows 38. C has 6 parts, so it shows 56. D has 8 parts, but they are not equal.

items.q: Which fraction is two thirds?
items.e: “two thirds” means 2 parts out of 3 equal parts: 23. The number of parts in the whole goes on the bottom.

items.q: Which fraction is three tenths?
items.e: “three tenths” means 3 parts out of 10 equal parts: 310. The number of parts in the whole goes on the bottom.

items.q: What fraction of the rectangle is shaded?
items.e: All 6 of the 6 equal parts are shaded: 66. That is the whole rectangle, 1 whole.

items.q: In the fraction 38, what does the 8 tell you?
items.e: The bottom number tells how many equal parts make the whole. In 38, the whole has 8 equal parts.

items.q: In the fraction 35, what does the 3 tell you?
items.e: The top number tells how many parts we count (for example, how many are shaded). In 35, 3 of the 5 equal parts are counted.

items.q: What fraction of the counters are green?
items.e: There are 3 counters in the set, so the bottom number is 3. 1 is green, so the answer is 13.

items.q: What fraction of the counters are green?
items.e: There are 4 counters in the set, so the bottom number is 4. 2 are green, so the answer is 24. Do not write 22: the bottom number is all the counters, not just the white ones.

items.q: What fraction of the counters are green?
items.e: There are 5 counters in the set, so the bottom number is 5. 3 are green, so the answer is 35. Do not write 32: the bottom number is all the counters, not just the white ones.

items.q: What fraction of the counters are green?
items.e: There are 6 counters in the set, so the bottom number is 6. 4 are green, so the answer is 46. Do not write 42: the bottom number is all the counters, not just the white ones.

items.q: What fraction of the counters are green?
items.e: There are 8 counters in the set, so the bottom number is 8. 5 are green, so the answer is 58. Do not write 53: the bottom number is all the counters, not just the white ones.

items.q: What fraction of the counters are not green?
items.e: 7 − 3 = 4 counters are white (not green) out of 7 counters. The answer is 47.

items.q: What fraction of the counters are not green?
items.e: 10 − 2 = 8 counters are white (not green) out of 10 counters. The answer is 810.

items.q: Leah has 5 apples. 2 are red and 3 are green. What fraction of the apples are red?
items.e: There are 5 apples in all, so the bottom number is 5. 2 are red: 25.

items.q: A bag has 10 marbles. 7 are blue. What fraction of the marbles are not blue?
items.e: 10 − 7 = 3 marbles are not blue, out of 10 marbles: 310.

items.q: Ryan has 8 hockey cards. 3 of them are Vancouver Canucks cards. What fraction of his cards are Canucks cards?
items.e: There are 8 cards in all, so the bottom number is 8. 3 are Canucks cards: 38.

items.q: Simran picks 7 flowers. 4 are pink and the rest are yellow. What fraction of the flowers are yellow?
items.e: 7 − 4 = 3 flowers are yellow, out of 7 flowers in all: 37.

items.q: Jasleen has 6 eggs. 13 of them are brown. How many eggs are brown?
items.e: 13 of 6 means 6 shared into 3 equal groups: 2, 2 and 2. So 2 eggs are brown. (3 is the number of groups, not the number in each group.)

items.q: What fraction of the counters is shaded?
items.e: The 12 counters are in 3 equal groups. One group out of 3 is shaded, so the shaded part is 13. (4 is the number of counters in each group, not the number of groups.)

items.q: What fraction of the counters is shaded?
items.e: The 10 counters are in 5 equal groups. One group out of 5 is shaded, so the shaded part is 15. (2 is the number of counters in each group, not the number of groups.)

items.q: What is 12 of 8?
items.e: Make 2 equal groups of the 8 counters. Each group has 4 counters. So 12 of 8 is 4.

items.q: What is 14 of 12?
items.e: Make 4 equal groups of the 12 counters. Each group has 3 counters. So 14 of 12 is 3.

items.q: What is 13 of 9?
items.e: Make 3 equal groups of the 9 counters. Each group has 3 counters. So 13 of 9 is 3.

items.q: What is 12 of 10 counters?
items.e: Share the 10 counters into 2 equal groups: 5 and 5. So 12 of 10 is 5.

items.q: Which picture shows 34 of the counters green?
items.e: 34 needs 4 counters in all with 3 green. That is picture D. A has 3 green and 4 white, so it shows 37. B shows 14. C has 4 green out of 7, so it shows 47.

items.q: Which picture shows 25 of the counters green?
items.e: 25 needs 5 counters in all with 2 green. That is picture B. A shows 35. C has 2 green and 5 white, so it shows 27. D has 4 counters, so it shows 24.

items.q: The bars are the same size. Which shaded part is bigger?
items.e: The top bar has 2 parts and the bottom bar has 4 parts. More parts means smaller parts, so 12 is bigger than 14.

items.q: The bars are the same size. Which shaded part is bigger?
items.e: The top bar has 8 parts and the bottom bar has 3 parts. More parts means smaller parts, so 13 is bigger than 18.

items.q: The bars are the same size. Which shaded part is bigger?
items.e: The top bar has 5 parts and the bottom bar has 10 parts. More parts means smaller parts, so 15 is bigger than 110.

items.q: The bars are the same size. Which shaded part is bigger?
items.e: The top bar has 6 parts and the bottom bar has 4 parts. More parts means smaller parts, so 14 is bigger than 16.

items.q: Compare the fractions. Choose <, > or =.
c: 18 < 14
18 = 14
18 > 14
items.e: Both fractions have 1 on top. A whole cut into 4 equal parts has bigger parts than a whole cut into 8 equal parts. So 18 < 14. 8 is bigger than 4, but 18 is smaller than 14.

items.q: Compare the fractions. Choose <, > or =.
c: 13 = 15
13 < 15
13 > 15
items.e: Both fractions have 1 on top. A whole cut into 3 equal parts has bigger parts than a whole cut into 5 equal parts. So 13 > 15.

items.q: Compare the fractions. Choose <, > or =.
c: 12 = 13
12 < 13
12 > 13
items.e: Both fractions have 1 on top. A whole cut into 2 equal parts has bigger parts than a whole cut into 3 equal parts. So 12 > 13.

items.q: Compare the fractions. Choose <, > or =.
c: 110 < 16
110 > 16
110 = 16
items.e: Both fractions have 1 on top. A whole cut into 6 equal parts has bigger parts than a whole cut into 10 equal parts. So 110 < 16.

items.q: Compare the fractions. Choose <, > or =.
c: 15 = 14
15 < 14
15 > 14
items.e: Both fractions have 1 on top. A whole cut into 4 equal parts has bigger parts than a whole cut into 5 equal parts. So 15 < 14.

items.q: Which unit fraction is the largest?
items.e: A unit fraction has 1 on top. The smallest bottom number means the biggest parts. 13 is the largest.

items.q: Which unit fraction is the smallest?
items.e: A unit fraction has 1 on top. The biggest bottom number means the smallest parts. 18 is the smallest.

items.q: Which unit fraction is the smallest?
items.e: A unit fraction has 1 on top. The biggest bottom number means the smallest parts. 110 is the smallest.

items.q: Order from least to greatest: 14, 12, 18
c: 14, 12, 18
18, 14, 12
12, 14, 18
18, 12, 14
items.e: Order from least to greatest. The biggest bottom number is the smallest fraction, so start with 18. The order is 18, 14, 12.

items.q: Order from least to greatest: 15, 110, 13
c: 110, 15, 13
110, 13, 15
13, 15, 110
15, 13, 110
items.e: Order from least to greatest. The biggest bottom number is the smallest fraction, so start with 110. The order is 110, 15, 13.

items.q: Ava’s group of 3 shares a pizza equally. Lucas’s group of 6 shares the same size pizza equally. Whose group gets bigger pieces?
items.e: A pizza shared by 3 people gives bigger pieces than one shared by 6 people. 13 > 16, so Ava’s group gets bigger pieces.

items.q: Owen’s group of 8 shares a pan of lasagna equally. Simran’s group of 5 shares the same size pan of lasagna equally. Whose group gets bigger pieces?
items.e: A pan of lasagna shared by 5 people gives bigger pieces than one shared by 8 people. 15 > 18, so Simran’s group gets bigger pieces.

items.q: Ji-woo’s group of 4 shares a cake equally. Mateo’s group of 10 shares the same size cake equally. Whose group gets bigger pieces?
items.e: A cake shared by 4 people gives bigger pieces than one shared by 10 people. 14 > 110, so Ji-woo’s group gets bigger pieces.

items.q: Which one is true?
c: 14 < 110
12 < 18
13 < 16
18 < 14
items.e: Check each one. A bigger bottom number means a smaller unit fraction. 18 < 14 is true, because 8 equal parts are smaller than 4 equal parts.

items.q: Which one is true?
c: 13 < 15
16 < 12
12 < 14
15 < 110
items.e: Check each one. A bigger bottom number means a smaller unit fraction. 16 < 12 is true, because 6 equal parts are smaller than 2 equal parts.

items.q: Which one is true?
c: 110 < 13
14 < 16
12 < 13
13 < 18
items.e: Check each one. A bigger bottom number means a smaller unit fraction. 110 < 13 is true, because 10 equal parts are smaller than 3 equal parts.

sets.title: Fractions on a number line and word problems

items.q: What fraction is at the red dot?
items.e: The line from 0 to 1 has 4 equal spaces, so each space is 14. The dot is 1 space from 0: 14. Count the spaces, not the tick marks.

items.q: What fraction is at the red dot?
items.e: The line from 0 to 1 has 3 equal spaces, so each space is 13. The dot is 2 spaces from 0: 23. Count the spaces, not the tick marks.

items.q: What fraction is at the red dot?
items.e: The line from 0 to 1 has 5 equal spaces, so each space is 15. The dot is 3 spaces from 0: 35. Count the spaces, not the tick marks.

items.q: What fraction is at the red dot?
items.e: The line from 0 to 1 has 6 equal spaces, so each space is 16. The dot is 5 spaces from 0: 56. Count the spaces, not the tick marks.

items.q: What fraction is at the red dot?
items.e: The line from 0 to 1 has 8 equal spaces, so each space is 18. The dot is 3 spaces from 0: 38. Count the spaces, not the tick marks.

items.q: What fraction is at the red dot?
items.e: The line from 0 to 1 has 10 equal spaces, so each space is 110. The dot is 7 spaces from 0: 710. Count the spaces, not the tick marks.

items.q: Which letter is at 610?
items.e: The line has 10 equal spaces, so each space is 110. Start at 0 and count 6 spaces. The letter there is A. Do not count the tick mark at 0.

items.q: Which letter is at 48?
items.e: The line has 8 equal spaces, so each space is 18. Start at 0 and count 4 spaces. The letter there is D. Do not count the tick mark at 0.

items.q: A pizza is cut into 8 equal slices. Liam eats 3 slices. What fraction of the pizza does he eat?
items.e: There are 8 equal slices, so the bottom number is 8. Liam eats 3: 38.

items.q: A cedar fence has 10 equal boards. Owen paints 7 of them. What fraction of the fence is painted?
items.e: 7 of the 10 equal boards are painted: 710.

items.q: A hiking trail in Stanley Park has 4 equal parts. Chloe’s family walks 3 parts. What fraction of the trail is left?
items.e: 4 − 3 = 1 part is left out of 4 equal parts: 14 of the trail.

items.q: Ava eats 13 of a sandwich. Sofia eats 16 of the same size sandwich. Who eats more?
items.e: Thirds are bigger than sixths, because a sandwich cut into 3 equal parts has bigger parts than one cut into 6. 13 > 16, so Ava eats more.

items.q: Arjun says 18 of a pizza is more than 14 of the same pizza, because 8 is more than 4. Is he right?
c: No. 14 is more.
items.e: A pizza cut into 8 equal slices has smaller slices than a pizza cut into 4. So 14 > 18.

items.q: Mei cuts a cake into 4 pieces. The pieces are different sizes. She says each piece is 14. Is she right?
c: No. Each piece is 13.
Yes. Each piece is one part.
No. The pieces are not equal.
items.e: Fourths must be 4 equal parts. The pieces are different sizes, so they are not fourths.

items.q: It is raining in Vancouver. 8 children play soccer, and 3 of them wear rain jackets. What fraction of the children wear rain jackets?
items.e: There are 8 children in all, so the bottom number is 8. 3 wear rain jackets: 38. (35 compares jackets with no jackets.)

items.q: Ethan sees 6 bald eagles. 12 of them sit in a cedar tree. How many eagles sit in the tree?
items.e: 12 of 6 means 6 shared into 2 equal groups: 3 and 3. So 3 eagles sit in the tree.

items.q: The Terry Fox Run route at school has 5 equal parts. Leah’s class walks 2 parts. What fraction of the route does the class walk?
items.e: 2 of the 5 equal parts: 25 of the route.

items.q: On Grouse Mountain, Zara skis 12 of a run. Kai skis 13 of the same run. Who skis farther?
items.e: 12 > 13, because halves are bigger than thirds. So Zara skis farther.

items.q: A garden bed has 6 equal parts. Hana plants beans in 4 parts. What fraction of the garden bed has no beans?
items.e: 6 − 4 = 2 parts have no beans, out of 6 equal parts: 26.

items.q: A basket has 10 peaches from the Okanagan. Noah eats 1 peach, then 1 more, then 1 more. What fraction of the peaches does he eat?
items.e: There are 10 peaches, so each one is 110 of the basket. Noah eats 3 peaches: 310.
